sections.h2: What is kept at the Grand Traverse County Register of Deeds in Traverse City?
sections.html:
Land paperwork for the whole county lands here: warranty and quitclaim deeds, mortgages, land contracts, liens and releases. The public can search every file. Scanned images are indexed back to 1966, and a clerk can pull older papers, some dating to 1853, when given a liber and page.

The clerks hand out no blank forms and cannot coach a seller through the wording. The county's own advice is to hire a Michigan real property lawyer, call a title agent, or complete a deed yourself, with the warning that forms downloaded from the web sometimes fail the recording rules.

The county spans 601 square miles, nearly a quarter of it water, and shares its name with the bay at Traverse City. A mission at Old Mission, founded in 1839, was the first permanent settlement. The territory was cut out in 1840 as Omeena County and renamed in 1851. A 2025 federal estimate of 96,729 residents is the largest count of any county in the northern Lower Peninsula.

sections.h2: Where do sellers find homes in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
Traverse City is the only city and the county seat. The villages of Fife Lake and Kingsley sit to the south and east, and Interlochen, Grawn and Chums Corner are unincorporated communities. Interlochen is home to the Interlochen Center for the Arts, a boarding school.

Water shapes the map. Long Lake is the biggest inland lake, the Boardman River runs west into West Bay at Traverse City, and the Old Mission Peninsula juts 17 miles into Grand Traverse Bay inside Peninsula Township. Part of the Pere Marquette State Forest lies within the county. A parcel on the peninsula, by a lake or in town is recorded at the same counter. Seven counties touch this one (Antrim, Kalkaska, Missaukee, Wexford, Manistee, Benzie and Leelanau), and a deed for land across the line goes to that county's own register.

Population climbed from 86,986 in 2010 to 95,238 in 2020 and 96,729 in the 2025 estimate, a gain of about 10,000 residents in fifteen years.

sections.h2: What does a seller pay at the Grand Traverse County recording counter?
sections.html:
Filing a deed, mortgage or lis pendens costs $30.00 whether it runs two pages or twenty. Mailed checks go to Register of Deeds or GTROD, with a stamped return envelope or $3.00 to cover postage.

Grand Traverse County recording price list
ItemCharge
One deed, mortgage or similar instrument$30.00
Each added instrument assigned or discharged$3
Treasurer certification, warranty deeds$5 for up to 25 parcels, then $0.20 each
Counter photocopies$1.00 per page, plus $5.00 to certify

The $30 figure traces to MCL 600.2567. The county's posted schedule is dated October 1, 2016, so phone the office before sending a large package.

sections.h2: How is the Grand Traverse County transfer tax worked out?
sections.html:
Clerks round the price up to the next $500 step and charge each step twice. The county levy is $1.10 for each $1,000, the 55 cents per $500 fixed by MCL 207.504 for a county this size. The state levy is $7.50 for each $1,000, which is the $3.75 per $500 in MCL 207.525. Together they take $8.60 from every $1,000 of rounded price.

The county's worked case is a $110,100 sale. Rounded to $110,500, it owes $828.75 to the state and $121.55 to the county, for $950.30. Add one dollar to the price and the base jumps to $111,000, producing $954.60. A house valued at the county median of $339,400 would round to $339,500 and owe about $2,919.70.

The deed either states the full price or comes with a value affidavit, and an exemption is written into the instrument. The exemption lists sit in MCL 207.505 for the county tax and MCL 207.526 for the state tax. They cover small transfers under $100, foreclosure deeds and gifts from parents to children or grandchildren, among others.

sections.h2: Why does the County Treasurer certify a warranty deed in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
Under MCL 211.135 a deed with a warranty covenant, or a land contract, cannot be recorded until the treasurer certifies two points: no tax liens are outstanding, and five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim with no covenant escapes this rule.

The Treasurer's office is at 400 Boardman Avenue, Suite 104, Traverse City, telephone 231-922-4735. Order the certification before the closing, because the register will hold the deed until it arrives.

The same elected official keeps the county's money, chairs the County Land Bank Authority, and runs the delinquent tax revolving fund that advances unpaid township and city taxes while the county pursues the owner. Each March the office starts collecting delinquent real property taxes. After a court order it can sell parcels that are more than 24 months behind, so a buyer or seller who sees an old balance on a parcel should get a written payoff first.

A seller who plans ahead can bring the following to the title company:

  • The Treasurer's certification, ordered ahead of the closing date.
  • A written payoff for any unpaid year, since the Treasurer collects delinquent bills from March 1 on.
  • The deed, drafted by a lawyer or title agent, because the register offers no drafting help.
  • A check for the $30.00 recording fee, the transfer tax and the $5 certification.

sections.h2: How quickly can unpaid tax cost an owner the property in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
Current bills go to the township, city or village treasurer from July 1 through February. When March arrives, whatever is still owed shifts to the County Treasurer.

Two years of delinquency end the owner's rights. In year one the county adds a 4% fee plus 1% interest each month. After forfeiture the rate rises to 1.5% monthly, counted back to the first missed date, and a $175 title search and notice costs join the total. The county files a certificate of forfeiture with the register, so any buyer's title search will find it. On March 31 a year after forfeiture the county forecloses, and it calls that step final.

  • Partial payments slow the interest, provided the last one arrives before foreclosure.
  • Owners get five notices: two ordinary letters, two certified letters and one hand delivery.
  • If an auction brings more than the debt, a former owner files a Notice of Claim by July 1 and asks the court for the surplus the following February.

The county adds a caution for people with escrow accounts: lenders occasionally miss a bill, especially right after a refinance, yet the owner stays liable.

sections.h2: What do the housing numbers look like in Grand Traverse County?
sections.html:
QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 lists a typical owned home at $339,400, with owners living in 77.2% of homes. Household income runs $81,647 at the median, rent $1,288, and one resident in four is 65 or older. The county has 40,287 households on 464 square miles of land.

Values at that level make transfer tax a noticeable line on a settlement statement. A seller with tenants, repairs or back taxes should order the treasurer's certification and a payoff letter first, so the title company can hand the register a clean deed.

faqs.q: What is the filing fee for a deed in Grand Traverse County?
faqs.a: $30.00 per document, whatever the page count. A sale adds transfer tax, and a warranty deed adds a $5 treasurer certification.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax does a Grand Traverse County sale pay?
faqs.a: $8.60 for every $1,000 of price rounded up to the next $500: $7.50 to the state and $1.10 to the county. A $110,500 base owes $950.30.

faqs.q: Can a deed be mailed to the Grand Traverse County register?
faqs.a: Yes. Enclose a check payable to Register of Deeds or GTROD plus a stamped, self addressed envelope, or add $3.00 for postage and handling.

faqs.q: When do overdue taxes move to the Grand Traverse County Treasurer?
faqs.a: March 1 after the bill year. The county then adds a 4% fee and 1% interest each month, and forfeiture follows a year later.

faqs.q: Will the Grand Traverse County register help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office provides no blank deeds and no drafting advice, so turn to an attorney or a title company.
